source_name: Slovenian business press — Forbes Slovenija / Večer / N1 banking coverage
why_relevant: Local press reliably reports these banks' results and strategy shifts within days, often ahead of the PDF annual report and with figures the banks do not headline (e.g. Delavska hranilnica's 2025 performance vs. plan, OTP Slovenia's revenue/profit growth). Good early-warning and interpretation layer.

source_name: Bankart — 'Aktualno' news / press release feed
why_relevant: The only official announcement channel for Bankart: management changes, TPP licensing, Payment Gateway launches, corporate stakes (e.g. Rekono). Directly matches the 'press releases' topic for the cell.

source_name: Bankart annual reports (Letno poročilo) PDF archive on wp-content
why_relevant: Audited annual reports carry transaction volumes, card counts, market shares, ownership by member banks and investment plans — the hardest quantitative baseline available for Slovenian card processing.

source_name: Bankart public payment-system rulebooks (Javni dokument za PS / Opis plačilnih sistemov)
why_relevant: Mandatory public disclosure documents describing BIPS, SIMP-PS and card settlement — participants, settlement cycles, risk framework. These are the authoritative technical description of Slovenian clearing and change with each scheme release.

source_name: Flik — official scheme site (flik.si)
why_relevant: Flik is the Slovenian domestic instant-payment scheme (P2P, P2M, Flik Pay, Flik POS) operated by Bankart with the banks. Scheme site carries participating-bank lists, product scope and FAQ changes that signal feature rollouts before any bank announces them.

source_name: Bankart Flik Pay merchant & Flik POS documentation
why_relevant: Merchant-facing onboarding docs reveal the commercial mechanics of Flik acceptance — gateway integration, merchant onboarding process, POS app capabilities. These are the operational detail behind 'payments modernisation' claims.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Poročilo o plačilnih in poravnalnih sistemih (annual payment & settlement systems report)
why_relevant: Annual report on payment and settlement systems gives per-system transaction volumes and values for BIPS, SIMP-PS, card settlement and TARGET-Slovenija, plus oversight assessments. Best single quantitative series for Slovenian payment infrastructure.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — payment statistics reporting framework and data
why_relevant: Defines what payment-statistics data Slovenian PSPs must report (card transactions, POS/ATM, instant payments) and links to the published aggregates — the upstream definition layer for any card/instant-payment market sizing.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Nacionalni svet za plačila (National Payments Council) e-news
why_relevant: Multi-stakeholder forum (central bank, banks, Bankart, merchants) whose e-newsletters explain upcoming scheme and regulatory changes in plain Slovenian. Excellent pointer source: names actors, projects and timelines that then become press releases.

source_name: European Payments Council — Register of Participants (SCT Inst) and Slovenia insight articles
why_relevant: Authoritative list of which Slovenian PSPs adhere to SCT Inst, plus an EPC insight article specifically describing the Slovenian instant-payment environment (BIPS-IP commercial, BIPS-IP P2P/P2M, Flik). Ideal for tracking scheme participation changes over time.

source_name: ECB — TIPS governance and MIP news (TARGET Instant Payment Settlement)
why_relevant: Bankart's BIPS connects to TIPS for reachability; ECB TIPS change requests, participant lists and MIP news reveal infrastructure changes that hit Slovenian banks before any local announcement. Also the digital-euro pipeline touching Slovenian rails.

source_name: Worldline — global media relations / press release archive (Slovenia-relevant items)
why_relevant: Worldline announces country-scoped product availability (e.g. 'Bank Transfer by Worldline' covering Slovenia) and acquiring/JV deals with banks. Such Slovenia mentions appear only in the group newsroom, never in Slovenian bank filings.

source_name: Nexi Group — investor relations & press releases (Nexi Slovenija d.o.o. parent)
why_relevant: Nexi Slovenija d.o.o. (Letališka cesta 29A, Ljubljana; ex-Nets CEE / ex-Intesa Sanpaolo Card / ex-Mercury Processing) is the second processing pole in Slovenia. Group IR and press material is where restructurings, country divestments and processing wins are disclosed.

source_name: Bizi.si / EBONITETE.SI / CompanyWall — Slovenian commercial company-data aggregators
why_relevant: Fast way to resolve entity identity, name history and parent structure for SI payment companies — these aggregators surfaced the full Nexi Slovenija rename chain (Nets CEE -> Mercury Processing -> Intesa Sanpaolo Card -> Nexi) and headline financials.

source_name: NLB Group — Bankart page in group markets/subsidiary disclosures
why_relevant: Bankart is bank-owned; NLB (its largest shareholder) describes Bankart's role, market shares and card/POS volumes in group material. This is the bridge between the processor and bank IR disclosure — useful cross-check on Bankart's own numbers.

source_name: Slovenian business/tech press covering payments (Delo, Monitor, Forbes Slovenija/N1, Cekin.si, 24ur)
why_relevant: Slovenian media carry Flik/Bankart milestones, user and transaction counts, and the European-payments-sovereignty debate (Flik vs Wero vs digital euro) that never appear in official releases. Monitor in particular covers technical detail of Flik Pay.

source_name: Slovenian bank Flik product pages (e.g. Intesa Sanpaolo Bank SI, NLB, SKB, Sparkasse, DBS, OTP)
why_relevant: Bank-level Flik and card product pages reveal which banks have joined the scheme, which Flik features (P2P, Flik Pay, Flik POS) each supports, and card scheme mix (Mastercard/Visa) — a distributed proxy for scheme rollout that is more current than the scheme site.

source_name: Mastercard Slovenia country site (mastercard.si)
why_relevant: Card scheme country presence; where Slovenia-specific scheme announcements, consumer research and acceptance initiatives would be published in Slovenian. Confirmed to exist as a localised sl-si tree.

source_name: ATVP (Agencija za trg vrednostnih papirjev) – registri in seznami, incl. MiCA/CASP
why_relevant: ATVP is the Slovenian competent authority for MiCA CASP authorisations and supervises Bitstamp Financial Services (MiFID firm, Ljubljana). Its registers and MiCA guidance are the authoritative Slovenian view of the crypto-adjacent licensed population.

source_name: ESMA MiCA public register of authorised CASPs
why_relevant: EU-level register of authorised CASPs and white papers; filterable by home member state, so it yields the Slovenian-authorised crypto firms and, conversely, the foreign CASPs passporting into Slovenia. Cross-check for ATVP.

source_name: EBA central register of payment and e-money institutions (PSD2 PIR)
why_relevant: Machine-readable EU-wide register of PIs/EMIs including Slovenian entities and their passporting footprint; better structured than the national HTML pages and good for automated change detection.

source_name: Bitstamp blog / newsroom (Bitstamp by Robinhood)
why_relevant: Primary corporate announcement channel of the Ljubljana-founded exchange (now Robinhood-owned; Bitstamp Financial Services Ltd. supervised by ATVP). Product, institutional-connectivity and licensing announcements land here first.

source_name: GoCrypto (Eligma) website – Slovenian-language pages
why_relevant: Slovenia's flagship crypto merchant-acceptance network; its own site carries merchant-coverage claims, product terms and market expansion pages. Merchant acceptance footprint is a leading indicator for crypto-at-POS trends relevant to payments vendors.

source_name: BTC d.d. – sporočila za medije (media releases)
why_relevant: BTC City Ljubljana is the anchor merchant partner of the Slovenian crypto-payments cluster (joint GoCrypto milestones). A listed retail/real-estate company whose media releases document merchant-side adoption events with dates.

source_name: NiceHash – company site and Slovenian media coverage cluster
why_relevant: Major Slovenian crypto-infrastructure company (hashpower marketplace + exchange/wallet features, Ljubljana/Maribor). Corporate blog plus dense Slovenian media coverage (RTVSLO, Delo, Siol, 24ur) make it trackable both directly and indirectly.

source_name: Startup Slovenija (startup.si) – Startup mapa: startupi & scaleupi, investitorji, novice
why_relevant: Official-ecosystem directory of Slovenian startups/scaleups with per-company profiles (Paywiser is listed) plus an investment-tagged news stream. Best single pointer for discovering wallet/BNPL/payment startups that never appear in licence registers.

source_name: Bloomberg Adria Slovenija – kripto trg / financni trgi desk
why_relevant: Only regional business-news desk covering Slovenian crypto licensing and payments substantively in Slovenian (e.g. first MiCA licence granted by ATVP; analysis of whether crypto payments are used in practice). Good for regulatory-event confirmation and market colour.

source_name: Siol.net – Digisvet / Posel danes
why_relevant: High-volume Slovenian tech/business desk that has repeatedly profiled the crypto-payments cluster (GoCrypto merchant acceptance, NiceHash recovery). Practical for spotting merchant-adoption anecdotes and new local players early.
